title: Tiny Dungeon Incremental (Claude), looking for feedback
author: teyhouse
selftext:
I had an idea for a small incremental game. Always wanted to make something with Three.js and Claude.

I have some prior experience from hobby projects in Unity and Godot. For this project, I wanted to find out how much AI can make development faster and how well this would work in a 2D Project.

  
**My role**

The game design and the mechanics are my work. All the systems and the balance are my decisions. Cluade wrote the code based on my instructions. I was more the game designer and director than the programmer. This was an interesting change for me. I am generally surprised how fast I was able to iterate and further develop this. I guess three.js was a good choice for Claude.  


**The game**

Tiny Dungeon Incremental is a pixel art idle game played in the browser. You hire adventurers and send them into dungeons. They bring back loot, and you sell it for gold. Later, you summon heroes (free Gacha), fight bosses and go through the Ages of Man based on Greek myth.  
  
**Assets**

The art, fonts and sounds are free assets from Kenney (CC0). The music is from Pixabay, except the first Intro Scene which was designed from ChatGPT based on a Prompt Claude made for me.

I have no plans for a big release. I want general feedback:

* How do the systems feel?
* Do the systems work well together?
* Do you see potential in the game?

You can test it on itch.io:  
[https://teyhouse.itch.io/tiny-dungeon-incrementel](https://teyhouse.itch.io/tiny-dungeon-incrementel)  
I recommend using fullscreen mode.

Looking forward to your feedback!

comments.author: thetinytrex
comments.body: Simple but fun! I didn't play it for too long only because I have other stuff to do but it seems pretty intuitive and straightforward. Systems seem to work well from my initial testing but I barely played for like 10 minutes.  In terms of potential, I don't see why not? There are a bajillion incremental games and this seem like a good enough one to scratch that itch. Although, I honestly don't know how it will fare in sales since the market is probably being flooded with incrementals.
